entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.decayRate

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.angularFrequency
entries.docstring:
The real frequency selected by the damping regime.

In the underdamped regime this is the oscillation frequency. In the critically damped
regime it is `0`. In the overdamped regime this is the real split rate between the two
roots.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def angularFrequency : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.discriminant_eq_four_mul_m_sq_mul_decayRate_sq_sub_ω_sq
entries.docstring: The relationship between the discriminant, decay rate, and natural angular frequency.
entries.snippet:
lemma discriminant_eq_four_mul_m_sq_mul_decayRate_sq_sub_ω_sq :
    S.discriminant = 4 * S.m^2 * (S.decayRate^2 - S.ω^2)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.decayRate_nonneg

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.isCriticallyDamped_decayRate
entries.docstring: A critically damped system has decay rate equal to the natural frequency.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gamma_eq_two_mul_m_mul_decayRate
entries.docstring: The damping coefficient is twice mass times the decay rate.
entries.snippet: lemma gamma_eq_two_mul_m_mul_decayRate : S.γ = 2 * S.m * S.decayRate

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.k_eq_m_mul_ω_sq

entries.snippet: lemma k_eq_m_mul_ω_sq : S.k = S.m * S.ω^2

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.k_eq_m_mul_decayRate_sq_of_criticallyDamped

lemma k_eq_m_mul_decayRate_sq_of_criticallyDamped (hS : S.IsCriticallyDamped) :

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.isOverdamped_decayRate
entries.docstring: An overdamped system has decay rate greater than the natural frequency.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.angularFrequency_eq_underdamped
entries.docstring: In the underdamped regime, the selected frequency uses the oscillation frequency.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularFrequency_eq_underdamped (hS : S.IsUnderdamped) :
    S.angularFrequency = sqrt (- S.discriminant) / (2 * S.m)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.angularFrequency_eq_criticallyDamped
entries.docstring: In the critically damped regime, the selected frequency is zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularFrequency_eq_criticallyDamped (hS : S.IsCriticallyDamped) :
    S.angularFrequency = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.angularFrequency_eq_overdamped
entries.docstring: In the overdamped regime, the selected frequency uses the real split rate.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularFrequency_eq_overdamped (hS : S.IsOverdamped) :
    S.angularFrequency = sqrt S.discriminant / (2 * S.m)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.angularFrequency_sq_of_underdamped

lemma angularFrequency_sq_of_underdamped (hS : S.IsUnderdamped) :

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.toUndamped_equationOfMotion
entries.docstring:

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.trajectory
entries.docstring:

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.trajectory_eq_of_underdamped
entries.docstring: In the underdamped regime, the selected trajectory uses the trigonometric base.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_eq_of_underdamped (IC : InitialConditions) (hS : S.IsUnderdamped) :
    S.trajectory IC =
      fun t : Time => exp (-S.decayRate * t) • S.underdampedBase IC t

entries.docstring: In the overdamped regime, the selected trajectory uses the hyperbolic base.

lemma trajectory_eq_of_overdamped (IC : InitialConditions) (hS : S.IsOverdamped) :
    S.trajectory IC =

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.exp_decay_smul_velocity
entries.snippet:
private lemma exp_decay_smul_velocity
    (a : ℝ) (y : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hy : Differentiable ℝ y) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t : Time => exp (-a * t.val) • y t) =
      fun t : Time => exp (-a * t.val) • (∂ₜ y t - a • y t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.exp_decay_smul_acceleration
entries.snippet:
private lemma exp_decay_smul_acceleration
    (a μ : ℝ) (y : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hy : Differentiable ℝ y) (hdy : Differentiable ℝ (∂ₜ y))
    (hy'' : ∂ₜ (∂ₜ y) = fun t => μ • y t) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (fun t : Time => exp (-a * t.val) • y t)) =
      fun t : Time => exp (-a * t.val) •
        (μ • y t - (2 * a) • ∂ₜ y t + a^2 • y t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.exp_decay_smul_equationOfMotion
entries.snippet:
private lemma exp_decay_smul_equationOfMotion
    (a μ : ℝ) (y : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hy : Differentiable ℝ y) (hdy : Differentiable ℝ (∂ₜ y))
    (hy'' : ∂ₜ (∂ₜ y) = fun t => μ • y t)
    (hγ : S.γ = 2 * S.m * a) (hk : S.k = S.m * (a^2 - μ)) :
    S.EquationOfMotion (fun t : Time => exp (-a * t.val) • y t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.criticallyDampedBase_velocity
ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.criticallyDampedBase_acceleration
ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.underdampedBase_velocity
entries.snippet:
private lemma underdampedBase_velocity (IC : InitialConditions) (hS : S.IsUnderdamped) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t : Time =>
      cos (S.angularFrequency * t.val) • IC.x₀ +
        (sin (S.angularFrequency * t.val) / S.angularFrequency) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀)) =
    fun t : Time =>
      (-S.angularFrequency * sin (S.angularFrequency * t.val)) • IC.x₀ +
        cos (S.angularFrequency * t.val) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.underdampedBase_acceleration
entries.snippet:
private lemma underdampedBase_acceleration (IC : InitialConditions) (hS : S.IsUnderdamped) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (fun t : Time =>
      cos (S.angularFrequency * t.val) • IC.x₀ +
        (sin (S.angularFrequency * t.val) / S.angularFrequency) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀))) =
    fun t : Time => -S.angularFrequency^2 •
      (cos (S.angularFrequency * t.val) • IC.x₀ +
        (sin (S.angularFrequency * t.val) / S.angularFrequency) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.overdampedBase_velocity
entries.snippet:
private lemma overdampedBase_velocity (IC : InitialConditions) (hS : S.IsOverdamped) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t : Time =>
      cosh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) • IC.x₀ +
        (sinh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) / S.angularFrequency) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀)) =
    fun t : Time =>
      (S.angularFrequency * sinh (S.angularFrequency * t.val)) • IC.x₀ +
        cosh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.overdampedBase_acceleration
entries.snippet:
private lemma overdampedBase_acceleration (IC : InitialConditions) (hS : S.IsOverdamped) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (fun t : Time =>
      cosh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) • IC.x₀ +
        (sinh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) / S.angularFrequency) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀))) =
    fun t : Time => S.angularFrequency^2 •
      (cosh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) • IC.x₀ +
        (sinh (S.angularFrequency * t.val) / S.angularFrequency) •
          (IC.v₀ + S.decayRate • IC.x₀))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle
entries.docstring:
A classical free particle with positive mass.

A free particle is a mechanical system evolving in the absence of
external forces. The dynamics are therefore entirely determined by
Newton's second law with zero force.

The only parameter of the system is the particle mass. The assumption
that the mass is strictly positive is physically natural and is used
throughout the development when simplifying the equation of motion.
entries.snippet:
structure FreeParticle where
  mass : ℝ
  mass_pos : 0 < mass

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.Trajectory
entries.docstring:
A trajectory is a time-dependent position function describing the motion
of the particle in one spatial dimension. Defining the trajectory.
entries.snippet: abbrev Trajectory

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.velocity
entries.docstring:
The velocity of a trajectory at a given time.
This is defined as the time derivative of the position function.
entries.snippet:
@[nolint unusedArguments]
noncomputable
def velocity (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.kineticEnergy
entries.docstring:
The kinetic energy of the free particle along a trajectory.

This is given by the classical expression `E = (1 / 2) m v²`,
where `m` is the particle mass and `v` is the velocity.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable
def kineticEnergy (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.NewtonsSecondLaw
entries.docstring:
Newton's second law for the free particle.

Since no external forces act on the particle, Newton's second law
reduces to the equation `m q'' = 0`, expressing that the acceleration
vanishes identically.
entries.snippet: def NewtonsSecondLaw (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory) (t : Time) : Prop

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.accel_zero
entries.docstring:
Newton's second law for a free particle implies that the acceleration
vanishes identically.

Since the particle mass is strictly positive, the equation
`m q'' = 0` can be simplified to `q'' = 0` by cancelling the mass
factor.
entries.snippet:
lemma accel_zero (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory) (h : ∀ t, s.NewtonsSecondLaw q t) :
    ∀ t, deriv (deriv q) t = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.velocity_const_of_zero_acc
entries.docstring:
If the acceleration of a trajectory vanishes everywhere, then the
velocity is constant.

More precisely, if the second derivative of the trajectory is zero
for all times, then there exists a constant `v₀` such that the
velocity is equal to `v₀` at every time.

The continuity assumption on `deriv q` is included to apply standard
results from real analysis relating vanishing derivatives to constant
functions.
entries.snippet:
@[sorryful]
lemma velocity_const_of_zero_acc (q : Time → ℝ) (h : ∀ t, deriv (deriv q) t = 0)
    (hcont : ContDiff ℝ 1 q) : ∃ v₀, ∀ t, deriv q t = v₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.FreeParticle.kineticEnergy_conserved
entries.docstring:
A free particle satisfying the equation of motion conserves kinetic energy.

The proof follows the standard argument from classical mechanics:
Newton's second law implies that the acceleration vanishes, which in
turn implies that the velocity is constant. Since the kinetic energy
depends only on the square of the velocity, it follows that the kinetic
energy is constant in time.
entries.snippet:
@[sorryful]
theorem kineticEnergy_conserved (s : FreeParticle) (q : Trajectory)
    (h : ∀ t, s.NewtonsSecondLaw q t) (hcont : ContDiff ℝ 1 q) :
    ∃ E, ∀ t, s.kineticEnergy q t = E

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.ofElectromagneticField_electricField
entries.docstring:

  `E` and the magnetic field `B` is `E`, as long as Gauss's law for magnetism and
  Faraday's law are satisfied.
entries.snippet:
lemma ofElectromagneticField_electricField {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (E : Time → Space 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (B : Time → Space 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (E_contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 ↿E) (B_contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿B)
    (B_grad : ∀ t, ∇ ⬝ (B t) = 0) (faraday : ∀ t x, curl (E t) x = - ∂ₜ (B · x) t) :
    (ofElectromagneticField c E B).electricField c = E

lemma toFieldStrength_eq_sub_tensorDeriv {d} {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}

    toFieldStrength A x =
    Tensorial.toTensor.symm (permT id PermCond.auto {η d | μ μ' ⊗ tensorDeriv A x | μ' ν}ᵀ)

    {η d | μ μ' ⊗ tensorDeriv A x | μ' ν}ᵀ)

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eq_sum_basis_eval
entries.docstring:
The statement that `F = F^{μν} eᵤ ⊗ eᵥ` written explicitly, with
  the components extracted via `toField`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eq_sum_basis_eval {d} {A : ElectromagneticPotential d} :
    A.toFieldStrength = fun x => ∑ μ, ∑ ν, toField {A.toFieldStrength x| [μ] [ν]}ᵀ •
      Vector.basis μ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Vector.basis ν

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eq_sum_basis
entries.docstring:
The statement that `F = F^{μν} eᵤ ⊗ eᵥ` written explicitly, with
  the components given by `∑ κ, (η μ κ * ∂_ κ A x ν - η ν κ * ∂_ κ A x μ)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eq_sum_basis {d} {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}
    (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.toFieldStrength x = ∑ μ, ∑ ν, (∑ κ, (η μ κ *  ∂_ κ A x ν - η ν κ * ∂_ κ A x μ)) •
      Lorentz.Vector.basis μ ⊗ₜ Lorentz.Vector.basis ν

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_eq_sum_basis_single
entries.docstring:
The statement that `F = F^{μν} eᵤ ⊗ eᵥ` written explicitly, with
  with the components given by `(η μ μ * ∂_ μ A x ν - η ν ν * ∂_ ν A x μ)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_eq_sum_basis_single {d} {A : ElectromagneticPotential d}
    (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    A.toFieldStrength x = ∑ μ, ∑ ν, (η μ μ * ∂_ μ A x ν - η ν ν * ∂_ ν A x μ) •
      Lorentz.Vector.basis μ ⊗ₜ Lorentz.Vector.basis ν

entries.name: Electromagnetism.ElectromagneticPotential.toFieldStrength_action_eq_sum
entries.docstring:
This lemma expresses the component form of the transformed field strength
tensor: when a Lorentz transformation Λ acts on the potential A, the resulting field strength
tensor's components are given by the standard tensor transformation rule involving the Lorentz
matrix elements Λ^μ_κ and Λ^ν_ρ applied to the original field components.
entries.snippet:
lemma toFieldStrength_action_eq_sum {d} (A : ElectromagneticPotential d) (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ A) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    (Λ • A).toFieldStrength x = ∑ μ, ∑ ν,
      (∑ κ, ∑ ρ, Λ.1 μ κ * Λ.1 ν ρ * toField {A.toFieldStrength (Λ⁻¹ • x) | [κ] [ρ]}ᵀ) •
      Vector.basis μ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Vector.basis ν

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.ClassicalContinuityEquation
entries.docstring:
Classical conservation of mass in conservative form, `partial_t rho + div (rho u) = 0`.

The equation is asserted at points where the time derivative of `rho` and the spatial
divergence of `rho u` are classical derivatives.
entries.snippet: def ClassicalContinuityEquation (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidState d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.SmoothContinuityEquation
entries.docstring:
A stronger continuity equation for globally differentiable fields.

This version records the first-order regularity needed by the classical continuity equation:
the density is differentiable in time, the mass flux `rho u` is differentiable in space, and
the continuity residual vanishes everywhere.
entries.snippet: def SmoothContinuityEquation (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidState d) : Prop

    SmoothContinuityEquation d fluid → ClassicalContinuityEquation d fluid

Conservation of momentum in conservative matrix-divergence form.

The equation is

`partial_t (rho u) + matrixDiv (rho u ⊗ u) = matrixDiv sigma + rho f`.

Here `stress` is intentionally not yet specialized to a Newtonian stress law.

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.timeDeriv_smul_velocity
entries.docstring: Product rule for the time derivative of a scalar field times a velocity field.
entries.snippet:
lemma timeDeriv_smul_velocity (d : ℕ) (rhoAtPosition : Time → ℝ)
    (velocityAtPosition : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : Time)
    (hRho : DifferentiableAt ℝ rhoAtPosition t)
    (hVelocity : DifferentiableAt ℝ velocityAtPosition t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t' => rhoAtPosition t' • velocityAtPosition t') t =
      rhoAtPosition t • ∂ₜ velocityAtPosition t + ∂ₜ rhoAtPosition t • velocityAtPosition t

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.timeDeriv_momentumDensity
entries.docstring: Product rule for the time derivative of the momentum density `rho u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma timeDeriv_momentumDensity (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidState d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hRho : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocity : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.velocity · x) t) :
    ∂ₜ (momentumDensity d fluid · x) t =
      fluid.rho t x • ∂ₜ (fluid.velocity · x) t + ∂ₜ (fluid.rho · x) t • fluid.velocity t x

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.spaceDeriv_momentumFlux_component
entries.docstring: Product rule for one spatial derivative of one component of `rho u ⊗ u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma spaceDeriv_momentumFlux_component (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidState d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i j : Fin d)
    (hMomentumDensity : Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d fluid t))
    (hVelocity : Differentiable ℝ (fluid.velocity t)) :
    ∂[j] (fun x' => momentumFlux d fluid t x' i j) x =
      fluid.velocity t x i • ∂[j] (fun x' => momentumDensity d fluid t x' j) x +
      ∂[j] (fun x' => fluid.velocity t x' i) x • momentumDensity d fluid t x j

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.matrixDiv_momentumFlux
entries.docstring: The matrix divergence of `rho u ⊗ u` split into continuity and convective parts.
entries.snippet:
lemma matrixDiv_momentumFlux (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidState d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hMomentumDensity : Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d fluid t))
    (hVelocity : Differentiable ℝ (fluid.velocity t)) :
    matrixDiv d (momentumFlux d fluid t) x =
      (∇ ⬝ momentumDensity d fluid t) x • fluid.velocity t x +
        fluid.rho t x • convectiveTerm d fluid t x

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.conservativeMomentumLHS_eq_convectiveMomentumLHS_add_continuityResidual_smul
entries.docstring:
The algebraic bridge between conservative and convective momentum.

The conservative momentum left-hand side equals the convective momentum left-hand side plus
the continuity residual times the velocity field.
entries.snippet:
lemma conservativeMomentumLHS_eq_convectiveMomentumLHS_add_continuityResidual_smul
    (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidState d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hRhoTime : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocityTime : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.velocity · x) t)
    (hMomentumDensity : Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d fluid t))
    (hVelocitySpace : Differentiable ℝ (fluid.velocity t)) :
    conservativeMomentumLHS d fluid t x =
      convectiveMomentumLHS d fluid t x + continuityResidual d fluid t x • fluid.velocity t x

entries.name: FluidDynamics.NavierStokes.momentumEquation_iff_convectiveMomentumEquation
entries.docstring:
The conservative and convective momentum equations are equivalent when the classical
continuity equation holds.

The differentiability assumptions are exactly the product-rule assumptions used to rewrite
`partial_t (rho u)` and `matrixDiv (rho u ⊗ u)`.
entries.snippet:
theorem momentumEquation_iff_convectiveMomentumEquation
    (d : ℕ) (data : FluidInMomentumBalance d)
    (hContinuity : ClassicalContinuityEquation d data.toFluidState)
    (hRhoTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (data.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocityTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (data.velocity · x) t)
    (hMomentumDensity : ∀ t,
      Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d data.toFluidState t))
    (hVelocitySpace : ∀ t, Differentiable ℝ (data.velocity t)) :
    MomentumEquation d data ↔ ConvectiveMomentumEquation d data

      + I * ⟪T (x + I • y), ↑(x + I • y)⟫_ℂ - I * ⟪T (x - I • y), ↑(x - I • y)⟫_ℂ) / 4

      - I * ⟪T (x + I • y), ↑(x + I • y)⟫_ℂ + I * ⟪T (x - I • y), ↑(x - I • y)⟫_ℂ) / 4

    (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j ∧ S.τ (c i) = c j) (m : Fin n)
    (p : Pure S c) (x : S.FD.obj (Discrete.mk (c (succSuccAbove i j m)))) :
    contrPCoeff i j hij (p.update (succSuccAbove i j m) x) =
    contrPCoeff i j hij p

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove
entries.docstring:
The embedding of `Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1 + 1)` which leaves a hole
  at `i` and `j`.
entries.snippet: def succSuccAbove (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (m : Fin n) : Fin (n + 1 + 1)

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_val
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_val (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (m : Fin n) :
    (succSuccAbove i j m).val = if m.1 < i.1 ∧ m.1 < j.1 then m.1
    else if m.1 + 1 < i.1 ∧ j.1 ≤ m.1 then m.1 + 1
    else if i.1 ≤ m.1 ∧ m.1 + 1 < j.1 then m.1 + 1
    else m.1 + 2

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_self_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_self_apply (i : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (m : Fin n) :
    succSuccAbove i i m = if m.1 < i.1 then ⟨m.1, by omega⟩ else ⟨m.1 + 2, by omega⟩

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_eq_succAbove_succAbove
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_eq_succAbove_succAbove (i : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
    succSuccAbove i (i.succAbove j) = i.succAbove ∘ j.succAbove

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_eq_predAbove
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_eq_predAbove {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    succSuccAbove i j = fun x => i.succAbove (((Fin.predAbove 0 i).predAbove j).succAbove x)

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_injective
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_injective {n : ℕ}
    (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) : Function.Injective (succSuccAbove i j)

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_eq_iff_eq
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma succSuccAbove_eq_iff_eq {n : ℕ}
    (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (m1 m2 : Fin n) :
    succSuccAbove i j m1 = succSuccAbove i j m2 ↔ m1 = m2

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_leq_iff_leq
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma succSuccAbove_leq_iff_leq {n : ℕ}
    (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (m1 m2 : Fin n) :
    succSuccAbove i j m1 ≤ succSuccAbove i j m2 ↔ m1 ≤ m2

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_lt_iff_lt
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma succSuccAbove_lt_iff_lt {n : ℕ}
    (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (m1 m2 : Fin n) :
    succSuccAbove i j m1 < succSuccAbove i j m2 ↔ m1 < m2

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_monotone
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma succSuccAbove_monotone {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) :

entries.snippet:

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_range
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma succSuccAbove_range {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (hij : i ≠ j) :

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_eq_orderEmbOfFin
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_eq_orderEmbOfFin {n : ℕ}
    (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    succSuccAbove i j = Finset.orderEmbOfFin {i, j}ᶜ
    (by rw [Finset.card_compl]; simp [Finset.card_pair hij])

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_symm
entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_symm (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) :

entries.name: Fin.permCond_succSuccAbove_symm

lemma permCond_succSuccAbove_symm {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → C} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1))

entries.snippet:

    (succSuccAbove i j) m = (Finset.orderIsoOfFin {i, j}ᶜ
      (by rw [Finset.card_compl]; simp [Finset.card_pair hij])) m

entries.snippet:
lemma succSuccAbove_image_compl {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (hij : i ≠ j)

    (succSuccAbove i j) '' Xᶜ = ({i, j} ∪ succSuccAbove i j '' X)ᶜ

entries.name: Fin.predPredAbove
entries.docstring:
The preimage of `m` under `succSuccAbove i j hij` given that `m` is not equal
  to `i` or `j`.
entries.snippet:
def predPredAbove (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j) (m : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (hm : m ≠ i ∧ m ≠ j) : Fin n

entries.name: Fin.predPredAbove_val
entries.snippet:
lemma predPredAbove_val (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j) (m : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (hm : m ≠ i ∧ m ≠ j) :
    (predPredAbove i j hij m hm).val = if m.1 < i.1 ∧ m.1 < j.1 then m.1
    else if m.1 - 1 < i.1 ∧ j.1 ≤ m.1 then m.1 - 1
    else if i.1 - 1 ≤ m.1 ∧ m.1 < j.1 then m.1 - 1
    else m.1 - 2

entries.name: Fin.succSuccAbove_predPredAbove
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma succSuccAbove_predPredAbove (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j) (m : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (hm : m ≠ i ∧ m ≠ j) :
    succSuccAbove i j (predPredAbove i j hij m hm) = m

entries.name: Fin.predPredAbove_eq_orderIsoOfFin
entries.snippet:
lemma predPredAbove_eq_orderIsoOfFin (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j) (m : Fin (n + 1 + 1))
    (hm : m ≠ i ∧ m ≠ j) :
    predPredAbove i j hij m hm =
    (Finset.orderIsoOfFin {i, j}ᶜ (by rw [Finset.card_compl]; simp [Finset.card_pair hij])).symm
    ⟨m, by simp [hm]⟩

entries.name: Fin.predPredAbove_injective
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma predPredAbove_injective (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (m1 m2 : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hm1 : m1 ≠ i ∧ m1 ≠ j) (hm2 : m2 ≠ i ∧ m2 ≠ j) :
    predPredAbove i j hij m1 hm1 = predPredAbove i j hij m2 hm2 ↔ m1 = m2

entries.name: Fin.predPredAbove_surjective
entries.snippet:
lemma predPredAbove_surjective (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (m : Fin n) : ∃ m' : Fin (n + 1 + 1), ∃ (h : m' ≠ i ∧ m' ≠ j),
    predPredAbove i j hij m' h = m

entries.name: Fin.predPredAbove_succSuccAbove
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma predPredAbove_succSuccAbove (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (m : Fin n) :
    predPredAbove i j hij (succSuccAbove i j m) (by simp) = m

  formed by dropping `i` and `j` in the source and their image in the target.

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.ComponentIdx.complexify_comp_succSuccAbove
entries.docstring:
`complexify` commutes with precomposition by `succSuccAbove`.
  We use `fun k => b (Fin.succSuccAbove i j k)` and direct application
  `(ComponentIdx.complexify b) (Fin.succSuccAbove i j m)` rather than composition so that
  dependent `ComponentIdx` types unify correctly (avoiding `Function.comp` type mismatch).
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ComponentIdx.complexify_comp_succSuccAbove
    {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → realLorentzTensor.Color}
    {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor) c) (m : Fin n) :
    (ComponentIdx.complexify (c := c ∘ Fin.succSuccAbove i j)
      (fun k => b (Fin.succSuccAbove i j k))) m =
    (ComponentIdx.complexify (c := c) b) (Fin.succSuccAbove i j m)

entries.name: Space.eq_grad_integral_of_curl_zero
entries.docstring:
A constructive form of the statement that if the curl of a function is zero,
  then it is equal to the grad of another function.

  In the context of e.g. electromagnetism the potential given by this lemma corresponds
  to that defined by the work done to move a unit charge from the origin to the
  point `x` along a straight line.
entries.snippet:
lemma eq_grad_integral_of_curl_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hcurl : curl f = 0) :
    f = grad (fun x => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ⟪f (t • x), basis.repr x⟫_ℝ ∂(volume))

entries.name: Space.matrixDiv
entries.docstring:
The divergence of a matrix-valued spatial field.

For a field `T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ`, `matrixDiv T` is the
vector field whose `i`th component is

`∑ j, ∂[j] (fun x => T x i j) x`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def matrixDiv (d : ℕ) (T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) :
    Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

entries.name: sandwichedTraceFunctional
entries.docstring:
The sandwiched trace functional `Q̃_α(ρ‖σ) = Tr[(σ^γ ρ σ^γ)^α]` where `γ = (1-α)/(2α)`.
This is the quantity underlying the sandwiched Rényi divergence:
`D̃_α(ρ‖σ) = log(Q̃_α(ρ‖σ)) / (α - 1)`.

Note: the `conj` operation gives `A.conj B = B * A.mat * B†`, and since `σ^γ` is Hermitian
(self-adjoint), `B† = B`, so `ρ.M.conj (σ.M ^ γ).mat = σ^γ * ρ * σ^γ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def sandwichedTraceFunctional (α : ℝ) (ρ σ : MState d) : ℝ

entries.name: f_alpha
entries.docstring:
The variational function `f_α(H, ρ, σ) = α · ⟪ρ, H⟫ − (α−1) · Tr[(σ^{−γ} H σ^{−γ})^{α/(α−1)}]`
where `γ = (1−α)/(2α)`. For fixed `H ≥ 0`, this is linear in `ρ` and convex in `σ`.
Frank–Lieb show that `Q̃_α(ρ‖σ) = sup_{H ≥ 0} f_α(H, ρ, σ)` for `α > 1`.

entries.name: rpow_mul_neg_rpow_eq_supportProj
entries.docstring:
For PSD `A` and `γ ≠ 0`, the product `A^γ * A^{-γ}` equals the support projection
of `A`. This is because `x^γ * x^{-γ} = if x = 0 then 0 else 1` for `x ≥ 0`.

entries.name: supportProj_mul_of_ker_le
entries.docstring:
The support projection of `A` acts as identity on `B` when `A.ker ≤ B.ker`.
Since `A.supportProj` projects onto `ker(A)⊥` and `B` is zero on `ker(A)`,
the projection preserves `B`.

entries.name: inner_eq_inner_conj_of_ker_le
entries.docstring:
Under the support condition `σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker` (i.e., supp(ρ) ⊆ supp(σ)),
conjugation by `σ^γ` and `σ^{-γ}` preserves the inner product:
`⟪ρ.M, H⟫ = ⟪σ^γ ρ σ^γ, σ^{-γ} H σ^{-γ}⟫`. This holds because the kernel condition
ensures `ρ` is supported on `supp(σ)`, where `σ^γ σ^{-γ}` acts as the identity.
entries.snippet:
lemma inner_eq_inner_conj_of_ker_le (ρ σ : MState d)
    (H : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hker : σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : γ ≠ 0) :
    ⟪ρ.M, H⟫_ℝ = ⟪ρ.M.conj (σ.M ^ γ).mat, H.conj (σ.M ^ (-γ)).mat⟫_ℝ

entries.name: f_alpha_le_at_optimizer
entries.docstring:
**Step 1c**: `H_hat` is a maximizer: for all `H ≥ 0`, `f_α(H) ≤ f_α(H_hat)`.
This uses the trace Young inequality: for PSD `A, B` and conjugate exponents `p, q > 1`,
`⟪A, B⟫ ≤ Tr[A^p]/p + Tr[B^q]/q`.
Applied with `A = σ^γ ρ σ^γ`, `B = σ^{-γ} H σ^{-γ}`, `p = α`, `q = α/(α-1)`,
the inner product identity `⟪ρ, H⟫ = ⟪A, B⟫` (under the support condition) yields
`f_α(H) ≤ Tr[A^α] = Q̃_α(ρ‖σ) = f_α(H_hat)`.
Note: the support condition `σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker` (i.e., supp(ρ) ⊆ supp(σ)) is necessary.
Without it, the theorem is false: taking ρ orthogonal to σ gives Q̃_α = 0 but
`f_α(H) = α · Tr[ρH] > 0` for appropriate H.
entries.snippet:
theorem f_alpha_le_at_optimizer (hα : 1 < α) (ρ σ : MState d)
    (H : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hH : 0 ≤ H) (hker : σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker) :
    f_alpha α H ρ σ ≤ f_alpha α (H_hat α ρ σ) ρ σ

entries.name: traceFunctional_eq_iSup_f_alpha
entries.docstring:
**Step 1 (Variational formula)**: For `α > 1`, the trace functional equals the
supremum of `f_α` over all PSD `H`:
  `Q̃_α(ρ‖σ) = ⨆ (H : HermitianMat d ℂ) (_ : 0 ≤ H), f_alpha α H ρ σ`.
The optimizer is `H_hat = σ^γ (σ^γ ρ σ^γ)^{α−1} σ^γ`.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceFunctional_eq_iSup_f_alpha (hα : 1 < α) (ρ σ : MState d) (hker : σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker) :
    Q̃_ α(ρ‖σ) = ⨆ (H : {H : HermitianMat d ℂ // 0 ≤ H}), f_alpha α H.1 ρ σ

entries.name: f_alpha_convex_in_sigma
entries.docstring:
(Convexity in σ): For fixed `H ≥ 0` and `ρ`, and `α > 1`, the map
`σ ↦ f_alpha α H ρ σ` is convex. The key is that for `p = α/(α−1) > 1`:
• `A ↦ Tr[A^p]` is convex on PSD matrices (trace function convexity, Theorem 2.10 of Carlen),
• `σ ↦ σ^{−γ} H σ^{−γ}` is *concave* in `σ` by Lieb concavity (since `−γ = (α−1)/(2α) ∈ (0,½)`),
• The composition of a convex non-decreasing function with a concave function is convex,
  but we actually need the sign: the second term has a factor `−(α−1) < 0` which
  flips concave → convex.
More precisely: `σ ↦ Tr[(σ^{−γ} H σ^{−γ})^p]` is concave (by Lieb + trace function convexity),
so `σ ↦ −(α−1) · Tr[(σ^{−γ} H σ^{−γ})^p]` is convex.
entries.snippet:
theorem f_alpha_convex_in_sigma (hα : 1 < α) (H : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hH : 0 ≤ H)
    (ρ : MState d) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (w : ι → ℝ) (hw_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hw_sum : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (σs : ι → MState d) (σ_mix : MState d)
    (hσ_mix : σ_mix.M = ∑ i, w i • (σs i).M) :
    f_alpha α H ρ σ_mix ≤ ∑ i, w i * f_alpha α H ρ (σs i)

theorem f_alpha_jointly_convex (hα : 1 < α) (H : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hH : 0 ≤ H)
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (w : ι → ℝ) (hw_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hw_sum : ∑ i, w i = 1)

    (hσ_mix : σ_mix.M = ∑ i, w i • (σs i).M) :
    f_alpha α H ρ_mix σ_mix ≤ ∑ i, w i * f_alpha α H (ρs i) (σs i)

    (w : ι → ℝ) (hw_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hw_sum : ∑ i, w i = 1)

entries.name: HermitianMat.ker_weighted_sum_le
entries.docstring:
If for all i, ker(σs i) ≤ ker(ρs i), then ker(∑ w i • σs i) ≤ ker(∑ w i • ρs i),

entries.snippet:
theorem HermitianMat.ker_weighted_sum_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (w : ι → ℝ) (hw_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i)

    (∑ i, w i • σs i).ker ≤ (∑ i, w i • ρs i).ker

entries.name: sandwichedTraceFunctional_jointly_convex
entries.docstring:
The trace functional `Q̃_α` is jointly convex for `α > 1`.
This is Proposition 3 of the paper, originally from Frank–Lieb.
The proof uses the variational formula:
  `Q̃_α(ρ‖σ) = sup_{H ≥ 0} f_α(H, ρ, σ)`
where `f_α(H, ρ, σ) = α · Tr[ρ H] - (α-1) · Tr[(σ^{-γ} H σ^{-γ})^{α/(α-1)}]`
is jointly convex in `(ρ, σ)` for fixed `H` (since the first term is linear and
the second uses the convexity of trace functions). The supremum of jointly convex
functions is jointly convex.
entries.snippet:
theorem sandwichedTraceFunctional_jointly_convex (hα : 1 < α) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (w : ι → ℝ) (hw_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hw_sum : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (ρs σs : ι → MState d) (ρ_mix σ_mix : MState d)
    (hρ_mix : ρ_mix.M = ∑ i, w i • (ρs i).M)
    (hσ_mix : σ_mix.M = ∑ i, w i • (σs i).M)
    (hker : ∀ i, (σs i).M.ker ≤ (ρs i).M.ker) :
    Q̃_ α(ρ_mix‖σ_mix) ≤ ∑ i, w i * Q̃_ α(ρs i‖σs i)

entries.name: exists_twirling_unitaries
entries.docstring:
A twirling set for the system `dB` exists: there is a finite collection of unitaries
whose average conjugation action twirls any matrix to a multiple of the identity.
Specifically, `(1/|κ|) Σ_i V_i X V_i† = (Tr X / dim dB) · I` for all Hermitian X on dB.
The standard construction uses the discrete Heisenberg-Weyl group of order `|dB|²`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma exists_twirling_unitaries [Nonempty dB] :
    ∃ (κ : Type) (_ : Fintype κ) (_ : Nonempty κ) (V : κ → Matrix.unitaryGroup dB ℂ),
      ∀ (X : HermitianMat dB ℂ),
        (Fintype.card κ : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i : κ, X.conj (V i : Matrix dB dB ℂ) =
          (X.trace / Fintype.card dB) • (1 : HermitianMat dB ℂ)

lemma conj_kron_one_entry (M : Matrix (dA × dB) (dA × dB) ℂ)
    (V : Matrix dB dB ℂ) (a₁ a₂ : dA) (b₁ b₂ : dB) :
    (Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) (1 : Matrix dA dA ℂ) V * M *
     (Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) (1 : Matrix dA dA ℂ) V).conjTranspose) (a₁, b₁) (a₂, b₂) =
    (V * (Matrix.of fun b₁' b₂' => M (a₁, b₁') (a₂, b₂')) * V.conjTranspose) b₁ b₂

entries.name: twirling_hermitian_entry
entries.snippet:
lemma twirling_hermitian_entry
    (κ : Type) [Fintype κ] (V : κ → Matrix.unitaryGroup dB ℂ)
    (hV : ∀ (X : HermitianMat dB ℂ),
      (Fintype.card κ : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i : κ, X.conj (V i : Matrix dB dB ℂ) =
        (X.trace / Fintype.card dB) • (1 : HermitianMat dB ℂ))
    (X : HermitianMat dB ℂ) (b₁ b₂ : dB) :
    ∑ i : κ, ((V i).val * X.val * (V i).val.conjTranspose) b₁ b₂ =
    (X.val.trace / (Fintype.card dB : ℂ)) * (Fintype.card κ : ℂ) *
      (if b₁ = b₂ then 1 else 0)

    (hV : ∀ (X : HermitianMat dB ℂ),
      (Fintype.card κ : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i : κ, X.conj (V i : Matrix dB dB ℂ) =
        (X.trace / Fintype.card dB) • (1 : HermitianMat dB ℂ))
    (X : Matrix dB dB ℂ) (b₁ b₂ : dB) :
    ∑ i : κ, ((V i).val * X * (V i).val.conjTranspose) b₁ b₂ =
    (X.trace / (Fintype.card dB : ℂ)) * (Fintype.card κ : ℂ) *
      (if b₁ = b₂ then 1 else 0)

entries.name: ker_le_traceRight
entries.docstring:
The kernel condition `σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker` is preserved under partial trace.
This follows because `supp(ρ) ⊆ supp(σ)` implies `supp(Tr_B ρ) ⊆ supp(Tr_B σ)`:
if `v ∈ supp(Tr_B ρ)`, then `⟨v, (Tr_B ρ) v⟩ > 0`, so for some basis vector `e_b`
we have `v ⊗ e_b ∈ supp(ρ) ⊆ supp(σ)`, hence `⟨v, (Tr_B σ) v⟩ ≥ ⟨v ⊗ e_b, σ (v ⊗ e_b)⟩ > 0`.

entries.name: sandwichedRenyiEntropy_mono_traceRight

The sandwiched Rényi divergence is monotone under partial trace for `α > 1`.
This follows from monotonicity of the trace functional together with the fact that
`D̃_α = log(Q̃_α) / (α - 1)` and both `log` and `1/(α-1)` are order-preserving for α > 1.

theorem sandwichedRenyiEntropy_mono_traceRight [Nonempty dB]
    (hα : 1 < α) (ρ σ : MState (dA × dB))
    (hker : σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker) :
    D̃_ α(ρ.traceRight‖σ.traceRight) ≤ D̃_ α(ρ‖σ)

entries.name: sandwichedRenyiEntropy_DPI_gt_one
entries.docstring:
The Data Processing Inequality for the Sandwiched Rényi relative entropy (α > 1).
Every CPTP map `Φ` satisfies `D̃_α(Φρ‖Φσ) ≤ D̃_α(ρ‖σ)`.

The proof uses the Stinespring representation (see `CPTPMap.exists_purify`):
every CPTP map can be written as ancilla preparation + unitary conjugation + partial trace.
Since the sandwiched Rényi divergence is invariant under the first two operations
(by additivity and relabel invariance) and monotone under partial trace
(by `sandwichedRenyiEntropy_mono_traceRight`), the DPI follows.
entries.snippet:
theorem sandwichedRenyiEntropy_DPI_gt_one (hα : 1 < α) (ρ σ : MState d₁) (Φ : CPTPMap d₁ d₂) :
    D̃_ α(Φ ρ‖Φ σ) ≤ D̃_ α(ρ‖σ)

entries.name: HilbertSchmidtOperatorSpace.hsInner_eq_pairSum

private lemma hsInner_eq_pairSum (X Y : L ℋ) :
    inner ℂ (ofOp X) (ofOp Y) =
      ∑ p : HSIndex ℋ × HSIndex ℋ,
        LinearMap.toMatrix (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis
          (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis Y.toLinearMap p.1 p.2 *
        star
          (LinearMap.toMatrix (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis
            (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis X.toLinearMap p.1 p.2)

      ∑ p : HSIndex ℋ × HSIndex ℋ,
        LinearMap.toMatrix (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis
          (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis Y.toLinearMap p.1 p.2 *
        star
          (LinearMap.toMatrix (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis
            (hsOrthonormalBasis (ℋ := ℋ)).toBasis X.toLinearMap p.1 p.2)

entries.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockOp_mul
entries.snippet:
private lemma blockOp_mul (A00 A01 A10 A11 B00 B01 B10 B11 : L ℋ) :
    blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) A00 A01 A10 A11 * blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) B00 B01 B10 B11 =
      blockOp (ℋ := ℋ)
        (A00 * B00 + A01 * B10)
        (A00 * B01 + A01 * B11)
        (A10 * B00 + A11 * B10)
        (A10 * B01 + A11 * B11)

private lemma blockOp_mul_blockDiagonal_zero_right
    (P00 P01 P10 P11 A Q00 Q01 Q10 Q11 : L ℋ) :
    blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) P00 P01 P10 P11 * blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) 0 A *
        blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) Q00 Q01 Q10 Q11 =
      blockOp (ℋ := ℋ)
        (P01 * A * Q10)
        (P01 * A * Q11)
        (P11 * A * Q10)
        (P11 * A * Q11)

entries.name: JensenOperatorInequality.rightEval_topLeft_scalar
entries.snippet:
private lemma rightEval_topLeft_scalar
    (r : ℝ) (R0 X T : L ℋ) :
    (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
        ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
          (-((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
            -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)))) =
      star X * (T * X) + r • (R0 * R0)

entries.name: JensenOperatorInequality.rightEval_bottomRight_scalar
entries.snippet:
private lemma rightEval_bottomRight_scalar
    (r : ℝ) (R1 X T : L ℋ) :
    (2⁻¹ * r) • (X * star X) +
        ((2⁻¹ * r) • (X * star X) +
          ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (R1 * (T * R1)) +
            (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (R1 * (T * R1)))) =
      (R1 * T * R1) + r • (X * star X)

private lemma hmiddle_leftMul_rightMul
    {s : ℝ} {A B : L ℋ}
    (hA : A ∈ pdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) (hB : B ∈ pdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) :
    cfcR (ℋ := HSOp ℋ) (fun x : ℝ ↦ x ^ s)
        (cfcR (ℋ := HSOp ℋ) (fun x : ℝ ↦ x ^ ((-1 : ℝ) / 2)) (rightMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) B) *
          leftMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) A *
          cfcR (ℋ := HSOp ℋ) (fun x : ℝ ↦ x ^ ((-1 : ℝ) / 2)) (rightMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) B)) =
      leftMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) (A ^ s) * rightMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) (B ^ (-s))

entries.snippet:
private lemma phiK_weightedSum_operatorPowerMean_eq
    {s θ : ℝ} (K A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ : L ℋ)
    (hA₁ : A₁ ∈ pdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) (hA₂ : A₂ ∈ pdSet (ℋ := ℋ))
    (hB₁ : B₁ ∈ pdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) (hB₂ : B₂ ∈ pdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) :
    phiK (ℋ := ℋ) K
        ((1 - θ) • operatorPowerMean (ℋ := HSOp ℋ) s 1
            (leftMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) A₁) (rightMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) B₁) +
          θ • operatorPowerMean (ℋ := HSOp ℋ) s 1
            (leftMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) A₂) (rightMulHS (ℋ := ℋ) B₂)) =
      (1 - θ) • liebTraceMap (ℋ := ℋ) s K A₁ B₁ +
        θ • liebTraceMap (ℋ := ℋ) s K A₂ B₂

LownerHeinzCore.square_convexity_diff_rhs
entries.snippet:
private lemma square_convexity_diff_rhs (A B : 𝓐) (u : ℝ) :
    (u * (1 - u)) • ((A - B) * (A - B)) =
      (u * (1 - u)) • (A * A) - (u * (1 - u)) • (A * B) - (u * (1 - u)) • (B * A)
        + (u * (1 - u)) • (B * B)

entries.name: LownerHeinzCore.square_convexity_diff_hCC_sum
entries.snippet:
private lemma square_convexity_diff_hCC_sum (A B : 𝓐) (u : ℝ) :
    ((1 - u) • A) * ((1 - u) • A)
      + ((1 - u) • A) * (u • B)
      + (u • B) * ((1 - u) • A)
      + (u • B) * (u • B) =
      ((1 - u) * (1 - u)) • (A * A) + ((1 - u) * u) • (A * B)
        + (u * (1 - u)) • (B * A) + (u * u) • (B * B)

    ((1 - u) • A + u • B) * ((1 - u) • A + u • B) =
      ((1 - u) * (1 - u)) • (A * A) + ((1 - u) * u) • (A * B)
        + (u * (1 - u)) • (B * A) + (u * u) • (B * B)

entries.name: LownerHeinzCore.square_convexity_diff
entries.snippet:
private lemma square_convexity_diff (A B : 𝓐) (u : ℝ) :
    (1 - u) • (A * A) + u • (B * B)
        - ((1 - u) • A + u • B) * ((1 - u) • A + u • B)
      =
      (u * (1 - u)) • ((A - B) * (A - B))

entries.name: HermitianMat.compoundHermitian_eigenvalues
entries.docstring:
The eigenvalues of `compoundHermitian A k` are the products of eigenvalues
of `A` over `k`-subsets, up to an index permutation.
entries.snippet:
lemma compoundHermitian_eigenvalues (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ σ : {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ≃ {S : Finset d // S.card = k},
      (compoundHermitian A k).H.eigenvalues ∘ σ =
        fun S => ∏ i : Fin k, A.H.eigenvalues (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

entries.name: HermitianMat.compoundHermitian_conj
entries.docstring:
`compoundHermitian` distributes over `HermitianMat.conj`: the compound of
`A.conj B` equals the conjugation of `compoundHermitian A k` by `compoundMatrix B k`.

lemma compoundHermitian_conj (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (B : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundHermitian (A.conj B) k =

      ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d),
        singularValuesSorted ((A ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).mat * B.mat) i ^ (2 * α)

entries.name: HermitianMat.scalarRpowApprox_eq_mul_integral_sub_integral
entries.snippet:
private lemma scalarRpowApprox_eq_mul_integral_sub_integral {x q T : ℝ}
    (hx : 0 < x) (hq : 0 < q) (hT : 0 < T) :
    scalarRpowApprox q T x =
      x * (∫ t in (0)..T, t ^ (q - 1) / (x + t)) -
        (∫ t in (0)..T, t ^ (q - 1) / (1 + t))

entries.name: HermitianMat.tendsto_mul_intervalIntegral_rpow_div_add
entries.snippet:
private lemma tendsto_mul_intervalIntegral_rpow_div_add {x q : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun T => x * (∫ t in (0)..T, t ^ (q - 1) / (x + t)))
      Filter.atTop
      (nhds (rpowConst q * x ^ q))

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace_mul_inv_shift_add_le
entries.snippet:
private lemma trace_mul_inv_shift_add_le {A B : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    (((A + B).mat * (A + B + t • 1).mat⁻¹).trace : ℂ) ≤
      ((A.mat * (A + t • 1).mat⁻¹).trace : ℂ) + ((B.mat * (B + t • 1).mat⁻¹).trace : ℂ)

entries.name: HermitianMat.trace_mul_inv_shift_eq_sum_div
entries.snippet:
private lemma trace_mul_inv_shift_eq_sum_div {A : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) {t : ℝ}
    (ht : 0 < t) :
    (((A.mat * (A + t • 1).mat⁻¹).trace : ℂ)).re =
      ∑ i, A.H.eigenvalues i / (A.H.eigenvalues i + t)

entries.name: HermitianMat.intervalIntegrable_weighted_trace_mul_inv_shift

      (fun t => t ^ (p - 1) * (((A.mat * (A + t • 1).mat⁻¹).trace : ℂ)).re)

entries.name: HermitianMat.tendsto_intervalIntegral_weighted_trace_mul_inv_shift
entries.snippet:
private lemma tendsto_intervalIntegral_weighted_trace_mul_inv_shift {A : HermitianMat d ℂ}
    (hA : 0 ≤ A) (p : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun T => ∫ t in (0)..T, t ^ (p - 1) * (((A.mat * (A + t • 1).mat⁻¹).trace : ℂ)).re)

theorem traceNorm_neg (A : Matrix m n R) : traceNorm (-A) = traceNorm A

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValues
entries.docstring: The trace norm of a square complex matrix is the sum of its singular values.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValues [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    A.traceNorm = ∑ i, singularValues A i

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValuesSorted
entries.docstring: The trace norm of a square complex matrix is the sum of its sorted singular values.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValuesSorted [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    A.traceNorm = ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card n), singularValuesSorted A i

entries.name: Matrix.singularValues_le_opNorm
entries.docstring: Every singular value is bounded by the operator norm.
entries.snippet:
theorem singularValues_le_opNorm [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (i : n) :
    singularValues A i ≤ ‖A‖

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_mul_le_opNorm_traceNorm
entries.docstring: The trace norm is bounded by the operator norm on the left times the trace norm on the right.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_mul_le_opNorm_traceNorm [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    (A * B).traceNorm ≤ ‖A‖ * B.traceNorm

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_conjTranspose
entries.docstring: The trace norm is invariant under conjugate transpose.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_conjTranspose (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    Aᴴ.traceNorm = A.traceNorm

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_mul_le_traceNorm_opNorm
entries.docstring: The trace norm is bounded by trace norm on the left times operator norm on the right.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_mul_le_traceNorm_opNorm [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    (A * B).traceNorm ≤ A.traceNorm * ‖B‖

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_sandwich_le
entries.docstring: Multiplication on both sides by contractions does not increase trace norm.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_sandwich_le [DecidableEq n] {S M T : Matrix n n ℂ} (hS : ‖S‖ ≤ 1)
    (hT : ‖T‖ ≤ 1) : (S * M * T).traceNorm ≤ M.traceNorm

entries.name: Matrix.abs_trace_le_traceNorm
entries.docstring: The absolute value of the trace is bounded by the trace norm.
entries.snippet:
theorem abs_trace_le_traceNorm (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    ‖A.trace‖ ≤ A.traceNorm

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_eq_max_re_tr_U
entries.docstring:
For square complex matrices, the trace norm is the maximum of `re (Tr[U * A])`
over unitaries `U`.
entries.snippet:
theorem traceNorm_eq_max_re_tr_U (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    IsGreatest {x : ℝ | ∃ U : unitaryGroup n ℂ, Complex.re ((U.val * A).trace) = x} A.traceNorm

entries.name: Matrix.traceNorm_add_le
entries.docstring: The trace norm satisfies the triangle inequality for square complex matrices.
entries.snippet: theorem traceNorm_add_le (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) : (A + B).traceNorm ≤ A.traceNorm + B.traceNorm

entries.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.traceNorm_eq_trace
entries.docstring: A positive semidefinite matrix has trace norm equal to its trace.
entries.snippet:
theorem PosSemidef.traceNorm_eq_trace {A : Matrix m m R} (hA : A.PosSemidef) :
    A.traceNorm = A.trace

entries.name: bargmannInvariantThree
entries.docstring:
The three-vertex Bargmann invariant: `⟨ψ₁|ψ₂⟩ · ⟨ψ₂|ψ₃⟩ · ⟨ψ₃|ψ₁⟩`.
    This is a gauge-invariant complex number whose argument is the
    geometric phase of the geodesic triangle.
entries.snippet: def bargmannInvariantThree (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) : ℂ

entries.name: bargmannPhaseThree
entries.docstring: The geometric (Pancharatnam-Berry) phase of three states.
entries.snippet: def bargmannPhaseThree (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) : ℝ

entries.name: bargmannInvariantThree_degenerate
entries.docstring: The Bargmann invariant of three identical states is 1.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma bargmannInvariantThree_degenerate (ψ : Ket d) :
    bargmannInvariantThree ψ ψ ψ = 1

entries.name: bargmannPhaseThree_degenerate
entries.docstring: The geometric phase of three identical states is 0.
entries.snippet:
lemma bargmannPhaseThree_degenerate (ψ : Ket d) :
    bargmannPhaseThree ψ ψ ψ = 0

entries.name: bargmannInvariantThree_reverse
entries.docstring: Reversing the cyclic order conjugates the invariant.
entries.snippet:
lemma bargmannInvariantThree_reverse (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) :
    bargmannInvariantThree ψ₃ ψ₂ ψ₁ = starRingEnd ℂ (bargmannInvariantThree ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃)

entries.name: bargmannPhaseThree_reverse
entries.docstring: Reversing the cyclic order negates the geometric phase (mod 2π).
entries.snippet:
lemma bargmannPhaseThree_reverse (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) :
    (bargmannPhaseThree ψ₃ ψ₂ ψ₁ : Real.Angle) =
    -(bargmannPhaseThree ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Real.Angle)

entries.name: bargmannInvariantThree_cyclic
entries.docstring: Cyclic permutation of the three states preserves the Bargmann invariant.
entries.snippet:
lemma bargmannInvariantThree_cyclic (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) :
    bargmannInvariantThree ψ₂ ψ₃ ψ₁ = bargmannInvariantThree ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃

entries.name: bargmannPhaseThree_cyclic
entries.docstring: Cyclic permutation preserves the geometric phase.
entries.snippet:
lemma bargmannPhaseThree_cyclic (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) :
    bargmannPhaseThree ψ₂ ψ₃ ψ₁ = bargmannPhaseThree ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃

entries.name: norm_bargmannInvariantThree_le_one
entries.docstring:
The Bargmann invariant has norm at most 1: each inner product factor
    is bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz on unit vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma norm_bargmannInvariantThree_le_one (ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃ : Ket d) :
    ‖bargmannInvariantThree ψ₁ ψ₂ ψ₃‖ ≤ 1

entries.name: BlochSphere.solidAngle
entries.docstring:
Solid angle of a geodesic triangle on the Bloch sphere, computed via
    the Van Vleck formula using `Complex.arg` for full-quadrant support.

    `Ω = 2 · arg(den + num · i)` where
    `den = 1 + n₁·n₂ + n₂·n₃ + n₃·n₁` and `num = n₁ · (n₂ × n₃)`.
entries.snippet: def solidAngle (p₁ p₂ p₃ : BlochSphere) : ℝ

entries.name: BlochSphere.dot_blochPoint
entries.docstring: The dot product of two Bloch points expressed in angle differences.
entries.snippet:
lemma dot_blochPoint (α₁ θ₁ α₂ θ₂ : ℝ) :
    (blochPoint α₁ θ₁ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ⬝ᵥ
    (blochPoint α₂ θ₂ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) =
    Real.sin α₁ * Real.sin α₂ * Real.cos (θ₂ - θ₁) +
    Real.cos α₁ * Real.cos α₂

lemma Braket.dot_swap_conj (ψ₁ ψ₂ : Ket d) :
    〈ψ₂‖ψ₁〉 = starRingEnd ℂ 〈ψ₁‖ψ₂〉
